ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure there are four input terminals A, B, C, D. A and B are connected to an upper rectangular logic block labeled “=1”; C and D are connected to a lower rectangular logic block labeled “=1”. The outputs of these two logic blocks are then connected to a third rectangular logic block on the right labeled “=1”, and the final output is Y. Reasoning: Each “=1” block means that when exactly one of the two inputs is 1, the output is 1, therefore it is equivalent to XOR. Let the upper intermediate output P = A XOR B, and the lower intermediate output Q = C XOR D, then the final Y = P XOR Q. According to the candidate combination ABCD = 1110: A=1, B=1, so P = 1 XOR 1 = 0; C=1, D=0, so Q = 1 XOR 0 = 1; finally Y = 0 XOR 1 = 1. Therefore when Y=1, the given combination is 1110.

Combine the cascade algebraically: Y=(A XOR B) XOR (C XOR D)=A XOR B XOR C XOR D. Thus Y=1 for input combinations with an odd number of 1 bits.
